{"id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-4c2fe49510c7", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "What is the difference between an Application Load Balancer and a Network Load Balancer?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-2bd115301bb3", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Both are Elastic Load Balancing types. They differ mainly in the network layer they work at and in the features that follow from that.

| | **Application Load Balancer (ALB)** | **Network Load Balancer (NLB)** |
|---|---|---|
| **OSI layer** | Layer 7 (application) | Layer 4 (transport) |
| **Protocols** | HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, WebSocket | TCP, UDP, TLS, TCP_UDP, QUIC |
| **Routing** | Content-aware. It routes on path, host header, HTTP headers, query strings, methods and source IP. | Connection-based. It routes on IP, port and protocol. |
| **Performance** | Good, but it inspects each request, so latency is higher. | Very high throughput, very low latency, and it handles sudden traffic spikes. |
| **IP addresses** | Dynamic IPs, so you use the DNS name. | One static IP per Availability Zone, and you can attach Elastic IPs. It also supports PrivateLink. |
| **Client IP preservation** | The client IP arrives in the `X-Forwarded-For` header. | The client source IP is preserved by default for instance targets. |
| **Targets** | Instances, IPs, Lambda functions and containers. | Instances, IPs and ALBs. It doesn't support Lambda targets. |
| **Security groups** | Supported. | Supported, but you have to enable them when you create the NLB. |
| **Built-in features** | Authentication with Cognito or OIDC, redirects, fixed responses, WAF integration, and weighted target groups. | TLS termination and PrivateLink endpoint services. |

**Choose an ALB when:**
- You run web apps, microservices or APIs over HTTP, HTTPS or gRPC.
- You need path-based or host-based routing, such as `/api` going to one service and `/web` to another.
- You want WAF, user authentication, or Lambda as a target.

**Choose an NLB when:**
- You need very high performance or ultra-low latency.
- You carry non-HTTP traffic such as gaming, IoT, VoIP, DNS or custom TCP/UDP protocols.
- You need static or Elastic IPs, for example when clients allow-list your IPs.
- You want to expose a service privately through PrivateLink.

You can also combine them. A common pattern puts an NLB in front of an ALB, which gives you static IPs and PrivateLink plus Layer 7 routing.

I can look at the load balancers in your connected AWS accounts if you'd like, for example to see which ones you run and how they're configured.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
